message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"3.51","text":"And it is evident that, even though the Scriptures lay open, he also sent people to scribes and teachers as people who knew the true things of the real law. And his also saying, “I did not come to annul the law,” while himself appearing to annul it, was the act of one indicating that the things he annulled were not part of the law. And by also saying, “Heaven and earth will pass away; one iota or a single stroke will certainly not pass away from the law,” he indicated that the things passing away before heaven and earth do are not part of the real law.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῶν γραφῶν προκειμένων","chosen":"even though the Scriptures lay open","rationale":"The genitive absolute describes the Scriptures as already lying before people or being available; “having been set forth” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"ὡς τοῦ ὄντως νόμου εἰδότας τὰ ἀληθῆ","chosen":"as people who knew the true things of the real law","rationale":"The participle describes the scribes and teachers; ὄντως distinguishes the genuine or actual law from material merely attributed to it."},{"source_quote":"σημαίνοντος ἦν","chosen":"was the act of one indicating","rationale":"The genitive is naturally read as a genitive of characteristic, describing what his apparently contradictory conduct signified."},{"source_quote":"ἰῶτα ἓν ἢ μία κεραία","chosen":"one iota or a single stroke","rationale":"κεραία denotes a small hornlike projection or written stroke; “serif” would be a more technical alternative."},{"source_quote":"τὰ πρὸ οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς παρερχόμενα","chosen":"the things passing away before heaven and earth do","rationale":"πρό is temporal here: these things pass away earlier than the promised passing of heaven and earth."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"3.52","text":"Since, then, while heaven and earth still remain, sacrifices, kingdoms, the “among those born of women” prophecies, and all such things have passed away because they were not commands of God—hence indeed he says, “Every planting that the heavenly Father did not plant will be uprooted”—for this reason he himself, being a true prophet, said, “I am the gate of life; the one who enters through me enters into life,” since no other teaching capable of saving exists. Therefore he also cried out, saying, “Come to me, all who toil,” that is, those who seek the truth and do not find it; and again, “My sheep hear my voice”; and elsewhere, “Seek and find,” since the truth does not lie plainly exposed.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"αἱ „ἐν γεννητοῖς γυναικῶν“ προφητεῖαι","chosen":"the “among those born of women” prophecies","rationale":"The quoted prepositional phrase is retained without supplying an unstated agent or referent; it may characterize the prophecies by their place among those born of women."},{"source_quote":"πᾶσα φυτεία","chosen":"every planting","rationale":"φυτεία can denote either a planting or what has been planted; “every plant” is a viable smoother alternative."},{"source_quote":"ἡ πύλη τῆς ζωῆς","chosen":"the gate of life","rationale":"πύλη denotes a gate or gateway; the genitive may be understood as a gate belonging or leading to life."},{"source_quote":"δεῦτε πρὸς μὲ πάντες οἱ κοπιῶντες","chosen":"Come to me, all who toil","rationale":"κοπιάω emphasizes laboring or becoming weary through labor; “all who are weary” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"ζητεῖτε καὶ εὑρίσκετε","chosen":"Seek and find","rationale":"Both forms can be read morphologically as indicatives or imperatives, but their setting as a direct exhortation supports imperatives; the Greek does not contain a future equivalent to “you will find.”"},{"source_quote":"ὡς μὴ προδήλως κειμένης τῆς ἀληθείας","chosen":"since the truth does not lie plainly exposed","rationale":"ὡς with the genitive absolute is taken causally. It could instead be rendered “on the understanding that the truth does not lie plainly exposed.”"}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"3.53","text":"But a voice bearing witness was also heard from the heavens, saying, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I delighted; listen to him.” And besides these things, wishing to expose them as having gone still further astray, he declared that the prophets—from whom they indeed insisted they had learned—had died desiring truth and without having learned it, saying, “Many prophets and kings desired to see what you see and to hear what you hear, and, amen, I tell you, they neither saw nor heard.” What is more, he said, “I am the one concerning whom Moses prophesied, saying, ‘The Lord our God raises up for you a prophet from among your brothers, like me as well; listen to him in all things. But whoever does not listen to that prophet will die.’”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐξ οὐρανῶν μάρτυς φωνὴ","chosen":"a voice bearing witness … from the heavens","rationale":"μάρτυς is a noun, literally presenting the voice as a witness; the rendering preserves that function without reducing it to merely “a heavenly voice.”"},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ πλεῖον αὐτοὺς πεπλανημένους ἐλέγξαι θέλων τοὺς προφήτας","chosen":"wishing to expose them as having gone still further astray, he declared that the prophets","rationale":"αὐτούς is taken as the object of ἐλέγξαι, while τοὺς προφήτας is the object of ἀπεφήνατο later in the sentence. Alternatively, τοὺς προφήτας could stand in apposition to αὐτούς, making the prophets themselves those exposed as astray."},{"source_quote":"παρ’ ὧν δὴ μεμαθηκέναι ἐβεβαίουν","chosen":"from whom they indeed insisted they had learned","rationale":"βεβαιόω here means to maintain or affirm firmly; the object of “learned” remains implicit as in the Greek."},{"source_quote":"ἐπιθυμοῦντας ἀληθείας καὶ μὴ μεμαθηκότας τελευτήσαντας","chosen":"had died desiring truth and without having learned it","rationale":"The participles characterize the prophets at death; “truth” supplies the natural object of “learned” from the immediately preceding genitive."},{"source_quote":"ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν","chosen":"amen, I tell you","rationale":"ἀμήν is retained rather than replaced with a harmonized familiar formula such as “truly I say to you.”"},{"source_quote":"Προφήτην ἐγείρει ὑμῖν κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν","chosen":"The Lord our God raises up for you a prophet","rationale":"ἐγείρει is printed as a present-tense form. It could function as a prophetic present with future sense, but the main rendering preserves the selected edition’s observable tense."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"3.54","text":"Therefore, without his teaching it is impossible to attain truth that saves, even if someone searches forever where the object of the search does not exist. But it was and is in the word of our Jesus. At any rate, knowing the true things of the law, when Sadducees asked on what grounds Moses had allowed seven to marry, he said, “Moses gave you permission because of your hardness of heart, for from the beginning it did not happen that way. For the one who created the human being from the beginning made him male and female.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἀληθείᾳ σωζούσῃ ἐπιστῆναι","chosen":"to attain truth that saves","rationale":"ἐφίστημι with the dative here conveys arriving at or coming upon something; σωζούσῃ explicitly characterizes the truth as saving."},{"source_quote":"κἂν τὸν αἰῶνά τις ζητῇ","chosen":"even if someone searches forever","rationale":"The accusative τὸν αἰῶνα expresses extended duration; “for an age” would preserve the noun more formally."},{"source_quote":"ἔνθα τὸ ζητούμενον οὐκ ἔστιν","chosen":"where the object of the search does not exist","rationale":"The substantival participle means “what is being sought”; the location introduced by ἔνθα is left general."},{"source_quote":"ἐν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἡμῶν λόγῳ","chosen":"in the word of our Jesus","rationale":"λόγος may mean his word, discourse, or teaching. The rendering preserves the genitival attachment to “our Jesus” without identifying Jesus himself as “the Word.”"},{"source_quote":"καθ’ ὃν λόγον Μωϋσῆς ἑπτὰ συνεχώρησεν γαμεῖν","chosen":"on what grounds Moses had allowed seven to marry","rationale":"καθ’ ὃν λόγον asks for the reason or principle. The seven are not explicitly called brothers or men in this wording, and no object of “marry” is supplied."},{"source_quote":"τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ ἐποίησεν αὐτόν","chosen":"the human being … made him male and female","rationale":"The selected wording has singular τὸν ἄνθρωπον and singular αὐτόν, followed by both “male and female”; the singular is preserved rather than changed to a plural familiar from other forms of the saying."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"3.55","text":"To those who suppose, as the Scriptures teach, that God swears, he said, “Let your yes be yes and your no, no, for anything beyond these comes from the evil one.” And to those who say that Abraham and Isaac and Jacob died, he said, “He is not God of the dead but of the living.” To those who think that God “tempts,” as the Scriptures say, he said, “The evil one is the one who tempts,” the same one who also tempted him. To those who assume that God does not know beforehand, he said, “For your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things before you petition him.” And to those who believe, as the Scriptures say, that he does not see everything, after saying, “Pray in secret,” he said, “And your Father, who sees secret things, will repay you.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὸ γὰρ περισσὸν τούτων","chosen":"anything beyond these","rationale":"τὸ περισσόν denotes what exceeds or goes beyond the stated yes and no; “the excess beyond these” would be more formally literal."},{"source_quote":"ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ","chosen":"from the evil one","rationale":"The genitive form can mean either “from evil” or “from the evil one.” The immediately following explicit ὁ πονηρός favors the personal rendering here."},{"source_quote":"οὐκ ἔστιν θεὸς νεκρῶν, ἀλλὰ ζώντων","chosen":"He is not God of the dead but of the living","rationale":"The implied subject is God from the preceding clause. The Greek describes the two groups substantivally as dead and living persons."},{"source_quote":"ὁ πονηρός ἐστιν ὁ πειράζων","chosen":"The evil one is the one who tempts","rationale":"πειράζω can mean either test or tempt, but attribution to the evil one and the following reference to his tempting Jesus support “tempt.”"},{"source_quote":"ὁ καὶ αὐτὸν πειράσας","chosen":"the same one who also tempted him","rationale":"The pronoun is retained as “him”; in context its most likely referent is Jesus, though the sentence does not rename him."},{"source_quote":"πρὶν αὐτὸν ἀξιώσητε","chosen":"before you petition him","rationale":"ἀξιόω most commonly concerns deeming worthy, but with a personal object it can carry the contextual sense of making a request or petition; “before you ask him” is a smoother alternative."},{"source_quote":"τὰ κρυπτὰ","chosen":"secret things","rationale":"The Greek is a substantival neuter plural, distinct from the preceding singular phrase ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ, “in secret.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακὼβ ἀπέθανεν","issue":"The selected text has the singular verb ἀπέθανεν after three coordinated names. This is a grammatical irregularity or singular agreement centered on the coordinated group; ordinary English requires the plural “died.”","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"τοῖς δὲ πιστεύουσιν (ὡς αἱ γραφαὶ λέγουσιν) ὅτι μὴ πάντα βλέπει, „ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ εὔχεσθε“ εἰπὼν „καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ βλέπων τὰ κρυπτὰ ἀποδώσει ὑμῖν“","issue":"The final construction uses the participle εἰπών but supplies no new finite speech verb before the second quotation. The preceding ἔφη is naturally understood by ellipsis, so the translation expresses it without emending the Greek.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
